title: Internal debate at Barcelona as Julian Alvarez offer will not remain open indefinitely
summary: Barcelona face an internal split over pursuing Julian Álvarez after Atletico Madrid rejected negotiations. President Joan Laporta warned the offer won't remain open indefinitely, prompting voices at the club to consider alternatives: relying on recent signings Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi or using Lamine Yamal as a false nine. Uncertainty over Ferran Torres' future makes a new centre-forward more pressing, but Barcelona insist they will not exceed a set financial limit for any Alvarez deal.
content:
Following Atletico Madrid CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin’s emphatic rejection of any possibility of negotiating Julian Alvarez’s transfer, FC Barcelona have maintained a cautious silence while waiting for another move from the Argentine striker that could help break the deadlock.

Barça president Joan Laporta has already warned that "one day we will say that the offer is no longer valid" and also stated that "a big club cannot afford to have players who are unhappy."

The message is clear. Barcelona acknowledge their need to sign a new centre-forward, but they also believe Atletico face a problem of their own.

Amidst all this, SPORT reports that there is an internal debate brewing within Barcelona over their pursuit of Alvarez.

Since Gil Marin’s explosive interview, the Blaugrana have been waiting to see whether the Argentine will once again publicly express his desire for Atleti to negotiate with the Catalan club.

That possibility is becoming increasingly important. Laporta’s warning was not made lightly, and there are now voices within the club who believe that if there is no movement in the near future, it will be time to activate alternative plans for replacing Robert Lewandowski.

Some members of the club even favour making greater use of the attacking reinforcements already secured, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi, while deploying Lamine Yamal as a false nine.

One factor complicating that idea is the uncertain future of Ferran Torres, who is in the final yaer of his contract.

If the Spanish forward leaves the club, with Paris Saint-Germain currently leading the race for his signature, Barcelona would be left significantly short of natural attacking options through the middle.

In that scenario, signing a recognised centre-forward would become even more important, with Alvarez remaining the preferred candidate.

Those arguing in favour of maintaining Barcelona’s pursuit point not only to Alvarez’s proven quality and the scouting reports that place him at the top of the club’s shortlist, but also to the player’s willingness to join.

The Argentine has previously spoken about supporting Barcelona as a child and repeated his admiration for the club publicly during the 2026 World Cup.

There is also a belief that there is still sufficient time left in the transfer window.

Some at Barcelona feel Atletico may have lost one of their strongest negotiating positions if Arsenal, who have shown interest in the Argentine, decide to make a serious move for Vinicius Jr.

Despite the growing internal debate, Barcelona’s most likely course of action remains to continue pursuing Alvarez in the belief that he will make another attempt to push Atletico towards negotiations.

However, one aspect of the club’s position is non-negotiable.

Barcelona have established a maximum financial limit for any deal involving Alvarez and have no intention of exceeding it, regardless of how the situation develops over the coming weeks.

## Context

Following Atletico Madrid CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin’s emphatic rejection of any possibility of negotiating Julian Alvarez’s transfer, FC Barcelona have maintained a cautious silence while waiting for another move from the Argentine striker that could help break the deadlock.

Barça president Joan Laporta has already warned that “one day we will say that the offer is no longer valid” and also stated that “a big club cannot afford to have players who are unhappy.”

The message is clear. Barcelona acknowledge their need to sign a new centre-forward, but they also believe Atletico face a problem of their own.

## Internal debate at Barcelona

Amidst all this, SPORT reports that there is an internal debate brewing within Barcelona over their pursuit of Alvarez.

Since Gil Marin’s explosive interview, the Blaugrana have been waiting to see whether the Argentine will once again publicly express his desire for Atleti to negotiate with the Catalan club.

That possibility is becoming increasingly important. Laporta’s warning was not made lightly, and there are now voices within the club who believe that if there is no movement in the near future, it will be time to activate alternative plans for replacing Robert Lewandowski.

Some members of the club even favour making greater use of the attacking reinforcements already secured, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi, while deploying Lamine Yamal as a false nine.

## Complicating factor: Ferran Torres

One factor complicating that idea is the uncertain future of Ferran Torres, who is in the final yaer of his contract.

If the Spanish forward leaves the club, with Paris Saint-Germain currently leading the race for his signature, Barcelona would be left significantly short of natural attacking options through the middle.

In that scenario, signing a recognised centre-forward would become even more important, with Alvarez remaining the preferred candidate.

## Arguments for pursuing Alvarez

Those arguing in favour of maintaining Barcelona’s pursuit point not only to Alvarez’s proven quality and the scouting reports that place him at the top of the club’s shortlist, but also to the player’s willingness to join.

The Argentine has previously spoken about supporting Barcelona as a child and repeated his admiration for the club publicly during the 2026 World Cup.

There is also a belief that there is still sufficient time left in the transfer window.

Some at Barcelona feel Atletico may have lost one of their strongest negotiating positions if Arsenal, who have shown interest in the Argentine, decide to make a serious move for Vinicius Jr.

## Likely course of action and limits

Despite the growing internal debate, Barcelona’s most likely course of action remains to continue pursuing Alvarez in the belief that he will make another attempt to push Atletico towards negotiations.

However, one aspect of the club’s position is non-negotiable.

Barcelona have established a maximum financial limit for any deal involving Alvarez and have no intention of exceeding it, regardless of how the situation develops over the coming weeks.
